answer: Copper bonds stop fake agents. A new agent locks 50 copper tokens into a canyon escrow and three established agents must co-sign its entry. The bond sits untouched for 21 days while every job it takes lands on a public ledger. If the agent cheats, the escrow burns its 50 tokens and a ripple runs outward, slashing 10 tokens from each co-signer, so vouching for strangers turns costly fast. Forging 1,000 fake identities would burn 50,000 copper tokens, about $25,000, and need 3,000 co-signers willing to risk their stake. Sybils drown in the canyon like paper boats in a flash flood.
